articles.title: Beyond the ballot: SA’s local elections are a test of governing competence
articles.dek: Beyond election promises to fix broken services, the real challenge for South Africa's incoming municipal councils lies in administrative competence, infrastructure maintenance, and surviving volatile coalitions.

articles.title: Fixing SA’s broken municipalities
articles.dek: As voters prepare to head to the polls, major political parties have unveiled competing manifestos to fix South Africa's collapsing municipalities, restore crumbling infrastructure, and eradicate corruption.

articles.title: Editorial: You can’t sweet-talk a dry tap
articles.dek: As municipal dysfunction and severe water shortages plague communities across South Africa, fed-up voters head into local government elections ready to punish failing leadership at the ballot box.

articles.title: Democracy for sale, delivery not included
articles.dek: As South Africa approaches the local government elections, political violence, corporate capture of parties, and collapsing municipal service delivery threaten the core of substantive democracy.

articles.title: IEC election readiness; equal to the task
articles.dek: Comparing election preparation to the intensity of the Soweto derby, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo outlines the systems, safeguards, and youth initiatives ensuring South Africa is ready for the local government elections.

articles.title: Turn grievance into a vote and mandate to deliver
articles.dek: Widespread service delivery failures have fuelled a crisis of grievance across South Africa. However, withdrawing from local elections only empowers the status quo; turning frustration into active democratic participation is the only route to municipal accountability.

articles.title: What citizens should look for in the polls
articles.dek: As South Africans prepare for local government elections, voters should look beyond manifesto promises to assess whether political parties possess the crucial capacity to recognise failure, coordinate effectively, and adapt responsibly.

articles.title: Water is a basic right – vote to defend it
articles.dek: Failing municipal infrastructure and contaminated taps are turning South Africa's water crisis into a violation of basic human rights. As local elections approach, voters must demand accountability from their leaders.

articles.title: Different ballots but the same poisoned water
articles.dek: Faced with failing infrastructure, poisoned water, and political indifference, South Africa's youth are turning away from the ballot box—not out of apathy, but out of a calculated refusal to validate broken promises.

articles.title: Your vote is written on the walls
articles.dek: At the 60th annual Sapoa convention, economists and property leaders debated how stagnant growth, failing infrastructure, and coalition politics are impacting South Africa's property sector ahead of crucial local elections.

articles.title: From ballot box to Just Energy Transition — participation without power
articles.dek: South Africa’s Just Energy Transition is reproducing a familiar democratic contradiction: communities are repeatedly invited to participate, while the power to determine their futures remains firmly in the hands of others.

articles.title: Emulate OR Tambo’s values

articles.title: Former Farmingdale State College Professor Antoine Munfakh charged with sexually abusing student
articles.dek: Antoine Munfakh pleaded not guilty to first-degree sexual abuse, third-degree rape and third-degree criminal obstruction of breathing during an arraignment before Suffolk Judge Evan S. Tanenbaum on Oct. 16.

articles.title: Spiking ambulance response times spur calls for real-time tracking
articles.dek: An ambulance in New York City now takes an average of 13 minutes to reach someone in life-threatening distress.
